API Authentication: Flow selection: Confidential Auth Code Grant = server-hosted app that CAN store a secret, user present. Public Auth Code Grant (+PKCE) = SPA / native app that CANNOT store a secret. JWT Grant = service integration, no user present, impersonates a user (RSA key pair). Implicit Grant = legacy, not recommended (use Public Auth Code instead).
Auth code is valid for only 120 seconds. Exchange it at /oauth/token immediately.
Confidential token request: header Authorization: Basic base64(integrationKey:secretKey) (colon, no spaces). Public (PKCE): no secret; send code_verifier in the body.
PKCE: random string (code_verifier) -> SHA-256 (S256) -> base64url = code_challenge; send code_challenge + code_challenge_method on /oauth/auth. Required for Public Auth Code Grant.
Token lifetimes: Auth Code access token = 8 hours. Refresh token = up to 30 days (Confidential) / 24 hours (Public). JWT access token = 1 hour, no refresh token: build a new JWT.
extended scope: refresh token expires 30 days from the LAST refresh (rolling). Without it: 30 days from original issue. Auth Code only.
JWT needs consent first (scope signature impersonation). After consent, the JWT payload scope lists only the API scopes you need (e.g. signature).
JWT payload: iss = integration key, sub = user ID (GUID), aud = account-d.docusign.com (demo) / account.docusign.com (prod), iat/exp (max 1 hour), scope. Header alg RS256.
After any flow: call /oauth/userinfo and use the account with is_default=true: take account_id and base_uri for every API URL.

Consent types: individual; admin consent for internal apps (Docusign Admin > Connected Apps); admin consent for external apps (scope=openid + admin_consent_scope). Admin consent needs Access Management + a claimed domain. Always build an individual-consent fallback.
Revoking consent invalidates refresh tokens. Live access tokens keep working until they expire. Reserved-domain users cannot revoke admin-granted consent.
Use the state parameter to prevent CSRF.

Confidential Auth Code vs Public Auth Code + PKCE: Can the app keep a secret? Server-side web app = Confidential (Basic base64(key:secret)). SPA / mobile / desktop = Public + PKCE (no secret, sends code_verifier).
Auth Code Grant vs JWT Grant: Is a user present to log in? Yes = Auth Code. No user / backend service / scheduled job = JWT (impersonates a user, RSA key).
Implicit Grant vs Public Auth Code + PKCE: Implicit is legacy and not recommended. For a browser or mobile app the answer is PKCE.
Consent scope vs JWT payload scope: JWT needs consent once with signature impersonation. Afterwards the JWT payload asks only for API scopes (e.g. signature).

Individual consent vs admin consent: Admin consent needs Access Management + a claimed domain. Internal app: Docusign Admin > Connected Apps. External app: openid + admin_consent_scope. Always keep individual consent as fallback.
Revoking consent: refresh token vs access token: Refresh tokens stop working at once; access tokens already issued keep working until they expire.
Auth host vs API base URI: Tokens come from account-d (demo) / account (prod). API calls go to base_uri from /oauth/userinfo (account with is_default=true).
Go Live Process: The old "20 API calls" requirement is gone. You can start Go-Live right after setting up the integration key.
Start Go-Live: Apps and Keys > Actions > Start Go live, then log in to the production account and select it. The submitter must be an admin of that production account.

Status (course wording): App is live or Pending approval (manual review, up to 48 hours). Developer Center wording: Under Review -> Review Passed -> Live; Declined = manual review (24-48 h); Review Expired if not promoted within 90 days.

Classification ("How will you use this integration?"): Private custom integration (your or your customers' employees), Third-party integration key (a partner app needs your own IK), Public integration (multi-customer, Partner Program), Embedded integration (ISV Embed: customers use your Docusign account). Must be set before Go-Live. An error listing no accounts means the integration type does not match the account type you logged into.
Developer-account envelopes are not legally binding; production envelopes are.

After Go-Live: switch to production auth (account.docusign.com) and production base URIs (from userinfo); re-create secrets/RSA keys and redirect URIs in production; template IDs differ between demo and production.
Hourly limit: default 3,000 calls/hour per account (shared by all apps), resets on the hour; excess calls are blocked. Burst: 500 per 30 seconds (prod), 200 (demo).
Polling: max one GET status per envelope every 15 minutes. Use Connect; for catch-up use listStatusChanges with overlapping time spans.
API Usage Center shows efficiency scores per app (Actions > View Efficiency Score) and lets admins raise the hourly limit (if the plan allows and apps are efficient).

Integration key classifications: Private custom integration = your/your customers' own employees. Third-party integration key = a partner app needs YOUR key. Public integration = sold to many customers (Partner Program). Embedded integration = customers use YOUR Docusign account (ISV Embed).
Go-Live error: no accounts listed: The integration type does not match the account type you logged into. It is not a permission or 20-calls problem.
Who submits Go-Live: Must log in to the production account and be an admin of it.
API Usage Center vs API Dashboard vs request logging: Usage Center = efficiency score + raise the hourly limit. Dashboard = failed requests, 90 days. Request logging = 50 raw logs for one user.
Hourly limit vs burst limit: 3,000/hour per account (resets on the hour) vs 500 per 30 seconds. Error names: Hourly_... / Burst_..._Limit_Exceeded.
Docusign Connect: Connect vs polling: pushed messages do not count against API limits, arrive only when something changes, and remove polling logic. Polling is limited to once per envelope per 15 minutes.
Organization-level: envelopes sent/received by all or selected accounts in the org; set up in Org Admin or the API; always JSON SIM.
Account-level: envelopes sent/received by all or selected users of one account; set up in eSignature Admin or the API (ConnectConfigurations).
Envelope-level: the eventNotification property on Envelopes:create, API only (not the Send page). It cannot cover envelopes received from external senders.

JSON SIM (Connect 2.0) is recommended for all apps: event-focused, smaller, customizable messages; supported at all levels. Legacy XML/SOAP and aggregate mode exist only at account and envelope level.
Securing the listener: HMAC signatures (X-DocuSign-Signature-1..n), Basic authentication, mutual TLS, OAuth 2.0 for Connect. Use HTTPS.
Retries: any non-2xx or timeout counts as a failure and is retried. Return 200 fast, process asynchronously (queue), and make processing idempotent.
Connected Fields verification results arrive via the extension-executed event, which is available only with JSON SIM.

Org vs Account vs Envelope level: Org = many accounts, Org Admin, JSON SIM only. Account = one account, eSignature Admin or ConnectConfigurations API. Envelope = eventNotification on Envelopes:create, API only, cannot cover envelopes received from others.
Connect vs polling: Connect messages do not count against API limits and arrive only on change. Polling: 1 per envelope per 15 min.
JSON SIM vs legacy XML / aggregate: JSON SIM (Connect 2.0) = recommended, smaller, works at all levels, needed for extension events. XML and aggregate = account and envelope level only.

HMAC vs Basic vs mutual TLS vs OAuth: HMAC (SHA-256, X-DocuSign-Signature-1) proves the payload came from Docusign and was not changed. Basic = username/password. mTLS = certificates at the transport layer. OAuth for Connect = token. Org-level Connect does not offer Basic auth.
Retries: Any non-2xx or timeout = failure, retried. Return 200 fast, process later (queue), make processing idempotent.
eSignature API: Request URL: {base_uri}/restapi/v2.1/accounts/{accountId}/envelopes; header Authorization: Bearer {token}.
Three envelope models: direct documents (documents + recipients + emailSubject + status), template reference (templateId + templateRoles + status), composite templates (compositeTemplates array).
Template reference is simple but cannot combine multiple templates. Composite templates can mix server templates, inline templates and documents in one envelope.

Composite templates: each object contributes at most one document; every serverTemplate/inlineTemplate needs a sequence; the composite object's own document property takes precedence. Best practice: supply documents with the composite document property, not the inline template.
status: sent sends immediately; created = draft (needed for document generation: create draft, fill docGen fields, then send).
Embedded signing: set clientUserId on the signer (status sent), then EnvelopeViews:createRecipient with matching email, userName, clientUserId, plus returnUrl and authenticationMethod.
Signing URL expires in 5 minutes and is single-use. Request it only when the user is ready to sign.

Focused view (recommended for basic cases) needs frameAncestors (your site + https://apps-d.docusign.com) and messageOrigins, plus Docusign JS. Use classic view for payment tabs, ID verification, some SBS providers, AI-Assisted Review, or 21 CFR Part 11.
returnUrl gets an event parameter (signing_complete, cancel, decline, ttl_expired, ...). Do not rely on it alone; confirm status via Connect.
Embedded sending: EnvelopeViews:createSender on a draft envelope lets the user tag and send inside your app.

Bulk send (v2.1): create a bulk send list -> create the envelope/template with a placeholder recipient -> (optional) test -> send the batch. Each recipient gets their own envelope from a queue. Watch queue limits and use Connect for status.
Void = permanent (PUT status=voided + voidedReason). Lock = temporary. You cannot update a completed recipient or add tabs to an envelope in a terminal state.
CORS lets a single-page app call the eSignature API from the browser; configure allowed origins in Apps and Keys. A back-end proxy is the alternative.
templateId + templateRoles vs compositeTemplates: One template = templateRoles. Combine several templates or templates + extra documents = composite templates.
status created vs sent: created = draft (needed for embedded sending and doc generation). sent = send now.
createRecipient vs createSender: createRecipient = embedded SIGNING URL (signer has clientUserId, status sent). createSender = embedded SENDING (user tags and sends a draft inside your app).
clientUserId set vs not set: With clientUserId the signer is embedded and gets no email. Values in createRecipient must match exactly (email, userName, clientUserId).
Focused view vs classic view: Focused = recommended, needs frameAncestors + messageOrigins and Docusign JS. Classic needed for payments, ID verification, some SBS, 21 CFR Part 11.
returnUrl event vs Connect: returnUrl's ?event=signing_complete is a hint only; confirm the status with Connect (or a GET).
Void vs lock: Void = permanent (status voided + voidedReason). Lock = temporary while you edit.
eSignature Features and Web Forms: Recipient auth options: access code (lightest, shared out of band), phone (call/SMS), KBA (public-record questions, US only), ID Verification (government photo ID / eID). Phone, KBA and IDV incur per-use fees.
IDV / phone in the API: add identityVerification.workflowId to the recipient; get the ID from IdentityVerifications:list (REST v2.1). IDV is not enabled by default in demo.
authenticationMethod on createRecipient only records your app's own authentication on the certificate. It does not enforce anything.

EU AES / QES (eIDAS): use identity verification configurations labeled EU AES / EU QES, or recipientSignatureProviders. SBS breaks some features: no Markup/Notary/fax attachment, combined PDF is unsigned, no field add/delete after the first signature.
Template-based web form = an envelope is generated after submission. Standalone = no envelope, data collection only.
Embedded web form instance: createInstance with clientUserId (required, max 100 characters); render the instance URL with Docusign JS; the envelope is created when the first user submits.

Sign right after submitting: embedded instance (clientUserId) + the submitter is the template's signer role; useFocusedViewForSigning only chooses focused vs classic view of that envelope. Signing by email = remote instance or the Initiate signing session from email setting (focused view unavailable with it).
Remote instance: sendOption + recipients[] with roleName; users get an email; the envelope is created when createInstance is processed.
Prefill priority: Docusign JS prefillValues (browser) override formValues sent in createInstance, which override the configuration default; read-only fields keep the createInstance value.
Prefill with formValues (field names from Configurations:getForm). Read results with Instances:getInstance: status (INITIATED / INPROGRESS / SUBMITTED / EXPIRED / FAILED), formValues, envelopes[].
Connected Fields send flow: TabInfo:GetConnectedFieldsTabGroups -> put the data in each tab's extensionData -> Envelopes:create.
ID Evidence API retrieves IDV evidence (ID images and events) for audit.
Access code vs phone vs KBA vs IDV: Access code = lightest, free, shared out of band. Phone = call/SMS. KBA = US only. IDV = government photo ID / eID, strongest. Phone, KBA, IDV cost per use.

identityVerification.workflowId vs authenticationMethod: identityVerification.workflowId (from IdentityVerifications:list) enforces IDV/phone. authenticationMethod on createRecipient only records how your app logged the user in.
Template-based vs standalone web form: Template-based = an envelope is created after submit. Standalone = no envelope, data only.
Embedded vs remote web form instance: Embedded = createInstance with clientUserId, show with Docusign JS. Remote = sendOption + recipients[] with roleName, user gets an email.

Connected Fields vs Data Verification: Connected Fields = signer fields bound to your own data model (Concerto types) and verified against your system. Data Verification = standard checks (bank account, SSN, email, phone, address, FEIN).

Web form prefill: Docusign JS prefillValues vs createInstance formValues vs default: Priority: Docusign JS prefillValues (browser) > formValues in createInstance > the configuration default. Exception: read-only fields keep the createInstance value. Users see stale data? Check the front end's prefillValues first.

Web form: sign in the same page vs signing email: In-session signing right after submit needs an embedded instance (createInstance with clientUserId, no sendOption/recipients) and the submitter must be the signer role in the linked template. useFocusedViewForSigning only switches focused vs classic look; it never causes an email. An email instead points to a remote instance or the configuration setting Initiate signing session from email (which also disables focused view).
Agreement Manager API: Agreement Manager uses AI (Docusign Iris) to extract structured data (parties, dates, provisions, obligations) from completed and imported agreements.
API use: list and search agreements, then getAgreement for one agreement's extracted fields and provisions; download documents when needed.
Legacy import: bulk-import existing (non-Docusign) agreements so AI extraction runs on them too.
Review loop: extracted values can be flagged for review. Build an external review step (or a workflow with branching rules) to validate and correct them before downstream use.
RAG: pull agreement data and documents through the API, index them in the AI system's retrieval store keyed by agreementId, and cite the source agreement in answers.
This is only 6% of the exam (~3-4 questions): focus on the use cases, not UI details.
GetAgreementsList vs GetAgreement: ID unknown / search / filter = GetAgreementsList. ID known, need parties + provisions = GetAgreement.

GetAgreement vs CreateAgreementSummary: Structured fields = GetAgreement. AI prose summary = CreateAgreementSummary (POST .../ai/actions/summarize). There is no getAgreementSummary. Only 4 operations: list, get, delete, createSummary.
Agreement data vs envelope data: Imported legacy agreements have no envelope, so Connect / Envelopes calls miss them. Extracted data is not the PDF file.
Workflow Builder and Workflow API: Start methods: Manually (Run Workflow in Docusign; users with Workflows: Prepare), From a link (URL to embed in a website or email; best for self-service intake), From an API call (your app triggers it), and event-based starts.
Trigger by API: get a token with aow_manage -> GetWorkflowTriggerRequirements (trigger URL and input schema) -> TriggerWorkflow with the inputs -> returns an instance ID (and a URL to embed).

Track and manage: getWorkflowInstancesList, getWorkflowInstance (status, times, started_by), cancelWorkflowInstance (stops one instance), pauseNewWorkflowInstances / resumePausedWorkflow (affect NEW instances only).

Common steps: Collect Data with Web Forms, Prepare eSignature Template, Send Documents for Signature (older name: Get Signatures), Identity Verification, branching rules (conditional paths), extension app steps (Data IO read/write, file output/archive).
Step order must match the business process, e.g. collect data -> verify identity -> sign -> archive.
Publish runs an automated check. Consent errors return a consentUrl: grant consent, then publish again. Errors must be fixed before publishing.
Extension apps in workflows must be installed/authorized in the account (App Center). Private distribution is for org-only apps.
Start: manually vs from a link vs from an API call: Staff run it in Docusign = manually. Public self-service intake on a website/email = from a link. Your app starts it = from an API call.
GetWorkflowTriggerRequirements vs TriggerWorkflow: First get the trigger URL + input schema (Requirements), then TriggerWorkflow with the inputs. Scope = aow_manage, not signature.
cancel vs pause / resume: cancelWorkflowInstance stops ONE running instance. pauseNewWorkflowInstances / resume affect only NEW instances; running ones continue.
Instance status: getWorkflowInstance = one instance's status. getWorkflowInstancesList = all instances.
Step names: Send Documents for Signature (older: Get Signatures), Collect Data with Web Forms, Prepare eSignature Template, Identity Verification.
App Center and Extension Apps: Extension apps connect third-party services INTO Docusign (verify data, read/write a system of record, archive files). They are published to the App Center (prod apps.docusign.com/app-center, demo apps-d.docusign.com/app-center).
Public = any App Center customer can install (choose publicationRegions). Private = only listed production accounts (org-specific data, e.g. connected fields against an internal DB).
Register in the Developer Console: form-based or by uploading/editing a JSON manifest. Manifest has connections, extensions (actionReferences), actions (connectionsReference), and distribution.

Lifecycle: register -> Console connection/extension tests -> functional tests -> submit for review -> publish (public: click to list in App Center; private: pick allowed accounts). Statuses: Draft, In Review, Approved, Rejected, Live, Discontinued.
Extension -> extension point: Connected fields + Data verification -> eSignature Add Fields and signing (email/phone verification also in Web Forms); Data IO and File output -> Maestro workflows.
Verification extensions: bank account (Verify.Version3.BankAccount), bank account owner (Verify.Version1.BankAccountOwner, US ABA only), email, phone, SSN, postal address, business FEIN.

Connected fields: on connect or refresh, Docusign calls GetTypeNames -> GetTypeDefinitions (Concerto data model); Verify runs when the signer fills the required fields. Results arrive via Connect extension-executed (JSON SIM).
File output cloud storage is for new apps; file archive is legacy.
Infrastructure: your HTTPS endpoint must be reachable by Docusign (firewall allow-list or API proxy); configure OAuth (tokenUrl, authorizationUrl, scopes) for Docusign's calls to you.
Extension -> extension point: Connected Fields + Data Verification -> eSignature (Add Fields / signing; email & phone verification also in Web Forms). Data IO + File output -> Maestro workflows.

Data IO vs File output vs Connected Fields vs Data Verification: Data IO = read/write records in a system of record (workflow). File output = send the finished file to storage. Connected Fields = signer fields from your data. Data Verification = check a value (bank, SSN...).
Public vs private distribution: Public = any App Center customer can install. Private = only listed production accounts (internal DB, org-only data).
Developer Console vs App Center: Register, test, submit in the Developer Console (form or JSON manifest). Install / list in the App Center.
Lifecycle: Register -> console tests -> functional tests -> submit for review -> publish. Statuses: Draft, In Review, Approved, Rejected, Live, Discontinued.
